name: Template: direct health (deaths and illness averted)
summary: TEMPLATE: what the charity does, where, the year modelled, the bottom line in years of healthy life per $1,000 (quote it live in the write-up), and the biggest uncertainty. If the result is more than ten times its cause's median on the site, say why ("more than ten times its peers because …").

source.title: charityevals' estimate: direct health (deaths and illness averted)

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Spending on the modelled program(s) in the year modelled
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: program expenses, in US dollars, for the activities modelled below and the same year as the reach numbers (say the year in the label and the summary). Cite the audited statement of functional expenses (or the annual report) and the page. Other currencies: a row in local currency times @fx.usd_per_<cur>_<year> (the IRS yearly average, else the World Bank's; add the fact with scripts/link-fx.py), never a typed rate.

rows.label: Total expenses (all programs, management, fundraising)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: total expenses for the same year, from the same document.

rows.label: Program expenses (all programs)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: program-service expenses for the same year, from the same document.

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ program expenses)
rows.explainer: Spreads management and fundraising over programs in proportion to their cost, as GiveWell and ACE do.

rows.label: Cost of the modelled program, including overhead
People reached in the year modelled

source.title: TEMPLATE: charity annual report / coverage survey

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: people who received the intervention in the year the spending covers (children dosed, people sleeping under nets distributed, infants vaccinated). Prefer independent coverage surveys to administrative counts; note which.

rows.label: Cost per person reached
rows.explainer: Context: compare with the charity's own figure and with other models of the family.

rows.label: Years of protection per person reached
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how long one round of the intervention protects a person (e.g. one dose, one net's useful life × usage).

rows.label: Annual mortality the intervention can reduce, in the target group
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: deaths per person-year from the causes the intervention affects, in the target age group and region, today, without the program. Use (or add) a country fact in facts/<country>.json (IHME GBD, UN IGME, DHS).

rows.label: Reduction in that mortality from the intervention
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: relative risk reduction from the best meta-analysis (Cochrane or equivalent); the 95% CI as low/high.

rows.label: Deaths malaria causes indirectly, per direct malaria death
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: where mortality_reduction is the fall in deaths from one cause, the deaths that cause brings on indirectly (through anaemia, low birth weight, other infections), per direct death: malaria @givewell.indirect_malaria_deaths_per_direct_malaria_death_2 (0.75, what the site's ranked malaria models read), diarrhoea @givewell_shared.indirect_deaths_per_direct_diarrhea_death. 0, with that reason, where mortality_reduction is the all-cause effect from the trials (it already holds them).

rows.label: Deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Direct and indirect deaths over the years of protection. If the intervention protects several age groups with different risks, replace this formula with one row per group and sum them here; check the result against the all-cause trial result per person-year, scaled to today's mortality.

rows.label: Share of deaths averted that are of children under five

source.title: TEMPLATE: WHO Global Health Estimates / IHME GBD

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the age split of the deaths averted: the split of deaths from the causes the intervention affects, in the countries it works in, weighted by its reach there. Source: WHO Global Health Estimates (deaths by cause, age, sex and country, the latest year) or IHME GBD. A split another model could reuse (one cause in one place) goes into facts/death_ages.json as `<cause>_<place>_share_<band>` (under5, 5_14, 15_49, 50plus) and is read here and below: share_5_14_of_over5 = @death_ages.<x>_share_5_14 / (1 - @death_ages.<x>_share_under5), and so on.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at five or older, share aged 5 to 14

source.title: TEMPLATE: WHO Global Health Estimates / IHME GBD

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the rest of the age split, band by band, so every death is valued at its own age band (docs/normalization.md 2.7), from the same source as share_under5. 0 when only under-fives are reached.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49

source.title: TEMPLATE: WHO Global Health Estimates / IHME GBD

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the rest at 50 to 74 (GiveWell's older weight also stands in above 74), from the same source.

rows.label: Illness averted, as a share of the mortality and income benefits
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: illness averted, as a share of the value of the deaths averted and the income gains together, the base GiveWell's supplementary adjustments apply to (uov_morbidity below). The site's one figure where it has one: malaria (nets, SMC) @givewell_common.malaria_morbidity; incentivised vaccines @givewell_common.morbidity_effects_from_directly_incentivized_vaccines_a. For another program, an estimate input (GBD disability weights, @gbd_disability_weights where the site has the weight, × cases averted × duration, against the deaths' and income's value), with its source; never DALYs × an exchange rate inside the model (docs/normalization.md INV-2). 0 with an explanation when illness is in unmodelled_benefits_adj instead; never both.

rows.label: Stillbirths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: for maternal and newborn programs, and nets and SMC protecting pregnant women: stillbirths averted per person reached, from the trial or meta-analysis. 0 with an explanation for programs that can't avert stillbirths.

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, ln(consumption) per year
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the yearly increase in ln(consumption) in adulthood from developmental effects (e.g. malaria or deworming and adult earnings), per person reached, undiscounted. 0 with an explanation when there is no evidence.

rows.label: Years until the income gain starts
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the site's one figure for the program (@givewell_shared.years_until_income_benefits_malaria, _smc, _iron or _deworming); for a program none fits, an estimate input from the study, with its source and range.

rows.label: Years the long-term income gain lasts
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for how long a long-term income gain lasts (GiveWell's working years, 40), read by every model that counts one (INV-13).

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, present value
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate, the wait included, so the result moves with it. Never type in a present value worked out elsewhere: rebuild it from its inputs.

rows.label: Resource sharing within households (multiplier on an earner's gain)
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (GiveWell's): an earner's income gain is shared with the household, so it counts this many times. Read by every model that values a long-term income gain (INV-13).

rows.label: Internal validity of the trials, a multiplier
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how far the trials measured the effect they report. The site's one figure where it has one for the intervention: malaria trials (nets, SMC) @givewell_common.internal_validity_adjustment_malaria; vitamin A and iron @givewell_common.internal_validity_adjustment_vas_iron; conditional incentives for vaccination @givewell_common.internal_validity_adjustment_new_incentives; water treatment @givewell_common.internal_validity_adjustment_for_morbidity. Otherwise a judgment input with a range, anchored on those.

rows.label: External validity: the trials' setting against this program's, a multiplier
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how far the trials' effect carries to this program today: other countries, lower baseline mortality, resistance (insecticides, drugs), another delivery model. 1 = the same setting; name the anchor (another model of this intervention) and the reason.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: The product of its two parts.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the outcome that would not have happened without the program (other providers, existing trends, government). Cite coverage data or trend data where possible.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: where other organisations contributed to the same outcome (co-funders, coalition campaigns, government delivery), this charity's share of everyone's spending on it. Others' in-kind work counts too: government staff time, partners' own delivery costs, and volunteers' unpaid time (beyond any stipend the charity pays, which is in its cost), valued at the local wage for the hours given. 1 when it delivers alone.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (fidelity, compliance, follow-through)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the reported reach that actually receives the intervention as studied: dose completion, coverage survey vs. reported.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: below 1 when other funders (governments, the Global Fund) would have paid for this work without the donation; above 1 when the donation pulls in other money. GiveWell's top charities typically sit at 0.85–0.95.

rows.label: Years a donation waits before the charity spends it
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the charity's unspent funds at year end ÷ its yearly spending (balance sheet and statement of activities), for a charity that grants or buys ahead from reserves; 0 for one that spends as it raises. Where the accounts show interest earned on the waiting funds, the dollar grows meanwhile: add a row interest_yield (interest income ÷ average cash and deposits, from the accounts) and multiply wait_discount by (1 + interest_yield) ^ gift_to_grant_years.

rows.label: Years from the charity's spending to the intervention reaching people
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: procurement, shipping and distribution: from the grant or purchase to the nets hung, the doses given (the charity's own distribution schedule, cited).

rows.label: Years from delivery to the middle of the protection
rows.explainer: The benefits come over the years of protection (a net's life, a season's doses), so they are discounted from its middle; 0 for a one-off effect such as a vaccine dose's.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the benefits come
rows.explainer: Every wait is discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit (the income gain's own wait is counted from delivery, in ln_income_gain_per_person).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Treatment costs averted, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (GiveWell's supplementary adjustment) for prevention programs: illness prevented saves its treatment. 0, with the reason, for a treatment program.

rows.label: Rebound malaria from lost immunity, as a share of value lost
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: malaria prevention only (nets, SMC, malaria vaccines): children protected build less immunity and catch more malaria later, a negative share (the site's one figure). 0, with the reason, for other programs.

rows.label: Investment of income increases, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: income gains partly invested and paying off later, the site's one figure per program: nets @givewell_shared.investment_of_income_increases_nets, vitamin A _vas, deworming _deworming, others @givewell_shared.investment_of_income_increases. 0, with the reason, when the model counts no income gain.

rows.label: Other benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: each effect not modelled above, with its sign and size: benefits positive (other diseases prevented), harms and risks (misuse, faster resistance, funging inside the organisation, monitoring errors) negative shares of value lost, added here, never a positive share subtracted elsewhere.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: GiveWell-style supplementary adjustments, each its own row, summed: they add to the modelled value as one share, as in GiveWell's sheets.

rows.label: Deaths averted
Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's moral weights for the age band of each death averted (under five, 5–14, 15–49, 50 and over), times your multiplier on the value of a life: the site's one value of a death (docs/normalization.md 2.7).

rows.label: Units of value from deaths averted
Units of value from stillbirths averted
rows.explainer: A stillbirth averted at the site's one value (@givewell_shared.uov_per_stillbirth, GiveWell's), times your multiplier on the value of a life.

rows.label: Units of value from later-life income
Units of value from illness averted
rows.explainer: A share of the deaths' and income's value, the base GiveWell's supplementary share has.

rows.label: Total units of value
rows.explainer: Illness and the other supplementary shares add to the modelled value side by side, as one sum of shares does in GiveWell's sheets.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the shared default for this kind of work (@staff_pay.share_goods; facts/staff_pay.json has one per kind: goods, staff-delivered, research and policy, advocacy, media). Where the charity's financials give salaries and benefits, use them instead: an estimate input (salaries ÷ total expenses, Form 990 Part IX lines 5–9) with its source.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the shared pay gap for this kind of work (@staff_pay.gap_local_delivery); pick the fact that fits the staff (local delivery, health and field, research and policy, advocacy, media, UK charity). Don't type a gap in.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid by cash donations
Units of value per dollar you give

output.label: Units of value per dollar you give
